title: Abraham Justified by Faith

questions.question: If Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not before whom?
options: God
Men
The angels
The law
questions.explanation: Romans 4:2 (ESV): "For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not before God."

questions.question: What does the Scripture say about Abraham's faith?
options: "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness."
"Abraham obeyed God, and his works proved his faith."
"Abraham offered his son out of faith, and God approved him."
"Abraham trusted the Lord, and became the father of nations."
questions.correctAnswer: "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness."
questions.explanation: Romans 4:3 (ESV): "For what does the Scripture say? 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.'"

questions.question: To the one who does not work but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as what?
options: Righteousness
A gift
Obedience
A wage
questions.explanation: Romans 4:5 (ESV): "And to the one who does not work but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness,"

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure does Paul cite as speaking of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works?
options: David
Moses
Isaiah
Elijah
questions.explanation: Romans 4:6 (ESV): "just as David also speaks of the blessing of the one to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:"

questions.question: The quote from David begins: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are ____."
options: covered
washed away
forgotten
pardoned entirely
questions.explanation: Romans 4:7 (ESV): "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;" (quoting Psalm 32:1).

questions.question: Was Abraham's faith counted to him as righteousness before or after he was circumcised?
options: Before he was circumcised
After he was circumcised
At the exact moment of his circumcision
The text says his obedience in circumcision completed his faith
questions.explanation: Romans 4:10 (ESV): "How then was it counted to him? Was it before or after he had been circumcised? It was not after, but before he was circumcised."

questions.question: Why did Abraham receive the sign of circumcision?
options: As a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised
As a requirement to become the father of the Jewish nation
As a condition of the covenant God established with him
As a symbol of his obedience regarding leaving his home country
questions.correctAnswer: As a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 (ESV): "He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised."

questions.question: Because Abraham was justified before circumcision, what title does he hold for those who believe without being circumcised?
options: He is the father of all who believe without being circumcised
He is the spiritual pattern for uncircumcised believers
He is the pioneer of the uncircumcised faith
He is the chief patriarch of all Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: He is the father of all who believe without being circumcised
questions.explanation: Romans 4:11 (ESV): "The purpose was to make him the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness would be counted to them as well,"

questions.question: The promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world did not come through the law, but through what?
options: The righteousness of faith
The covenant of circumcision
The election of grace
The shedding of blood
questions.explanation: Romans 4:13 (ESV): "For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world did not come through the law but through the righteousness of faith."

questions.question: Paul writes, "For if it is the adherents of the law who are to be the heirs, faith is null and the promise is void." What does the law bring?
options: Wrath
Knowledge of sin
Condemnation
Death
questions.explanation: Romans 4:15 (ESV): "For the law brings wrath, but where there is no law there is no transgression."

questions.question: Why does the promise depend on faith?
options: In order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring
So that no one can boast in their works before God
Because faith is the only thing a human can truly offer God
To show that the law was only a temporary measure for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: In order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring
questions.explanation: Romans 4:16 (ESV): "That is why it depends on faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring..."

questions.question: Abraham believed in the presence of the God who gives life to the dead and does what?
options: Calls into existence the things that do not exist
Brings light out of the darkest shadows
Makes a way where there is no way in the wilderness
Declares the end from the very beginning
questions.correctAnswer: Calls into existence the things that do not exist
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17 (ESV): "...God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls into existence the things that do not exist."

questions.question: "In hope he believed against hope, that he should become the father of many nations..." What did Abraham not do regarding God's promise when he considered his own body (as good as dead) or the barrenness of Sarah's womb?
options: He did not weaken in faith
He did not complain to God
He did not try to fulfill it through Hagar again
He did not waver concerning the timing
questions.correctAnswer: He did not weaken in faith
questions.explanation: Romans 4:19 (ESV): "He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, which was as good as dead... or when he considered the barrenness of Sarah's womb."

questions.question: Instead of growing weak, what happened to Abraham due to his faith?
options: He grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God
He rejoiced in the Lord day by day waiting for the promise
He received new vitality in his physical body
He was fully assured that God would raise Isaac if necessary
questions.correctAnswer: He grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God
questions.explanation: Romans 4:20 (ESV): "No unbelief made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God,"

questions.question: Paul concludes that the words "it was counted to him" were not written for Abraham's sake alone, but for ours also. Righteousness will be counted to us who believe in whom?
options: Him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord
Jesus Christ, the Son of God who loves us
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
The Spirit of grace who dwells within us
questions.correctAnswer: Him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord
questions.explanation: Romans 4:24 (ESV): "but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord,"

key_verse_text: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness."
